text:
sam: Quick heads up — noticed duplicate text in the onboarding sample UI when a streaming connection reconnects. Happens when EventSource reconnects and the SDK replay logic applies Last-Event-ID.
leo: can you paste repro? I've seen dupes but assumed app concat bug.
sam: steps: open sample-app, force auth refresh (rotate token) mid-stream so EventSource reconnects. Sometimes we get the last chunk twice in the UI.
anya: interesting — are we deduping by seq or resume token on the client? Some SDKs replay the last event when reconnecting if Last-Event-ID is present.
sam: logs from runtime: ```
[2141-03-01T10:00:01Z] runtime: emit seq=27 resume=tok-27 data="...hello"
[2141-03-01T10:00:01Z] runtime: keepalive
[2141-03-01T10:00:01Z] proxy: close->reopen (auth refresh)
[2141-03-01T10:00:01Z] runtime: emit seq=28 resume=tok-28 data="world"
```
Browser flow: EventSource sets Last-Event-ID=27 on reconnect and server resends seq=27/28. Our sample-app handler blindly appends incoming chunks, so "...hello" is shown twice.
leo: ah — so the server is resending last event (seq 27) which is normal SSE semantics if Last-Event-ID requested the last id. Other SDKs dedupe by comparing the seq field and ignoring already-processed seq numbers.
anya: which SDKs implement dedupe? node SDK has a small in-memory last-seq check, python/go don't. We need parity. Also edge case: if we accept up-to-last-seq on reconnect but the first event after reconnect is a partial continuation of the previous chunk, dedupe can remove needed bytes.
sam: exactly — sometimes seq=27 was a partial JSON fragment and seq=27 resent completes the JSON when combined with seq=28. If client dedupes by seq alone we drop necessary bytes.
leo: so dedupe must be aware of fragment semantics: either dedupe only whole-final events (have type: chunk/final) or perform an idempotent merge strategy keyed by resume token + seq + byte-offset.
anya: short-term mitigations for sample-app: 1) prefer resume tokens (opaque) rather than Last-Event-ID for reconnect semantics; 2) on reconnect, request server to resend from seq+1 if possible, or have server emit explicit `event: resume` with a placement marker; 3) client-side: implement a small reassembly buffer that can accept a resent seq and merge overlapping bytes rather than drop them.
sam: what's feasible? We want a fast onboarding fix (sample-app) plus an SDK parity plan.
leo: for sample-app: implement reassembly buffer + prefer resume tokens. If Last-Event-ID present, do not drop identical seqs immediately; instead detect overlap by checking if concatenating yields valid JSON before dropping. That covers partial-fragment cases.
anya: for SDKs: add a common helper in the SDK core: sseReconnectHelper(options) that exposes safeReassembleOnReconnect semantics. We'll add it to JS SDK first then port. Include tests for: (a) full duplicate events, (b) duplicate partial events where duplicate completes JSON, (c) overlapping bytes.
sam: infra note — proxy closes/reopens during auth refresh causing SSE reconnection spikes. We should try to make reconnects transparent or do a short grace period where reconnects are handled with resume tokens rather than Last-Event-ID resends.
infra-bot: INFRA-402 created to trace auth-refresh proxy close patterns and consider in-proxy sticky behavior.
leo: also document in DX: "Reconnect semantics & idempotency" with recommended server signals: `event: seq`, `event: resume`, and `event: final`, plus explicit byte-offset or fragment id if payloads may split.
anya: will draft SDK PR and a small README note for sample-app. For now I'll add defensive logic to sample-app: buffer on reconnect + try-merge on seq duplicates.
sam: thanks. small follow-up: can we add telemetry that logs when a reconnect causes identical seqs to be delivered and whether client dedupe was applied? would help tune heuristics.
leo: good idea — lightweight metric: reconnect_duplicate_seq_count per-client. Add opt-in flag in sample-app.
sam: ok I'll open PR for sample-app today. Thanks all :+1:
